keywords: how do i write a function
entries.response: function name(parameter) { return something; } — the name is what you call it by, the parameter is the input, and return sends a value back out. Nothing after return runs.
If a test shows 'got undefined', your function ran but never hit a return statement — the logic might be right, it's just not being sent back. Add return in front of the value.
A boolean is just true or false. A comparison like amount > 10000 already produces one — you can return it directly, no need for an if statement just to say 'if this is true, return true'.

> means strictly greater than (10000 itself doesn't count). >= means greater than or equal to (10000 itself does count). Read the brief's exact wording — 'over' and 'or more' mean different things here.
if (condition) { return x; } if (otherCondition) { return y; } return z; — checks run top to bottom, and the first one that matches wins. Put the most specific condition first.

keywords: what does the test console show
entries.response: Each row calls your function with specific input and checks whether what it actually returns matches what's expected. A red cross shows you exactly what your function returned, so compare that against what it should have been.
Text comparisons in JavaScript are case-sensitive — 'Flagged' and 'flagged' are different values. Match the exact spelling and capitalisation shown in the brief.
The function name in your code has to match exactly what's expected — check for typos, and make sure you haven't accidentally renamed it while editing.
